About Helion

We are a fusion power company based in Everett, WA, with the mission to build the world's first fusion power plant, enabling a future with unlimited clean electricity. Our vision is a world with clean, reliable, and affordable energy for everyone.

Since Helion's founding in 2013, we have raised $1.5 billion from long-time investors such as Sam Altman, Mithril, and Capricorn Investment Group as well as new investors including Thrive Capital, LightSpeed Venture Capital, SoftBank, and others to propel us forward. Our current prototype, Polaris, has reached record-breaking plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius (13 keV). Helion is continuing to iterate and on the path to the world's first fusion power plant, Orion.

This is a pivotal time to join Helion. You will tackle real-world challenges with a team that prizes urgency, rigor, ownership, and a commitment to delivering hard truths – values essential to achieving what no one has before. Together, we will change the future of energy, because the world can't wait.


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Fusion happens in the power electronics, and at the frontier of what Helion is building, the hardest problems don't have textbook answers. As a Principal Power Electronics Engineer, you'll own those problems — the highest-risk, least-defined pulsed-power and power-conversion challenges the program faces — and set the technical direction that the rest of the electrical organization builds on. Before the iPhone existed, Apple went to America's wireless carriers with terms none of them had ever granted: no carrier logo on the device, no carrier software, and control over how it was sold. Verizon walked away. Cingular said yes, reportedly before it had seen a working prototype, and on January 9, 2007 became the exclusive U.S. carrier for a phone the public had not yet seen. Apple gave up the reach of every other carrier, Cingular gave up control it had never surrendered, and both got something worth more. No template could have produced that agreement. People with the relationships, the nerve and a structure in mind did.

(Fun fact. Most people think it was A&T, but “Cingular” was the one who negotiated and announced it, and “AT&T” is what the carrier was called by the time the phone shipped in June 2007. That’s why most people say “the AT&T and iPhone deal.”)

At Mercury, we are looking for the person who will do that for us. We are building the financial layer for ambitious people of all kinds, and the platforms where they already work are where we want to be: the default bank for AI, the core banking* partner for merchants. We expect the nature of work is changing, and a leader paired with AI tools and the autonomy to build can create 10x outcomes: modeling deals, shaping integrations with our product teams and standing up the function as you go. Bring your relationships, and we will bring the product, the team and the room to build something that doesn't exist yet.

As a Senior Structures Engineer - Advanced Analysis on the Target Area team, you will be responsible for ensuring the structural integrity over repeated operational cycles of the hardware subjected to impulse loads. The currents from our pulsed power system and the rapid energy release from high-gain targets impart electromagnetic forces, shocks to target-facing structures. You will leverage advanced modeling to predict these highly nonlinear loads, design force-resilient structures, and validate your models through real-world testing to help us build a fusion chamber that survives repetitive impulse loads.
